position.summary: During the week of October 10-14, 2026, Italy's parliament approved a new electoral law that opposition parties immediately branded a 'scam' designed to lock Meloni's coalition in power through 2027. The government opened budget talks with banks and energy groups over their contribution to the 2027 fiscal plan, while Goldman Sachs warned of bond risks and the EU pressed for fiscal prudence. Italy and the European Commission edged toward a natural-gas price cap deal. Pope Leo XIV announced he would undergo lung surgery in the coming days for a localized nodule. Intesa Sanpaolo sweetened its 34-to-35-billion-euro bid for Monte dei Paschi and warned rivals. A tornado struck Marsala and Petrosino in Sicily, and Pfizer announced roughly 330 job cuts at its Sicily plant. Prosecutors requested a trial for Campari chairman Luca Garavoglia over a 1.29-billion-euro tax-evasion allegation. Thieves stole approximately 30,000 bottles worth five million euros from the Antinori winery in Tuscany. Thousands marched in Rome around the Gaza ceasefire anniversary. NATO launched its ten-day Steadfast Noon nuclear exercise hosted by Italy. KKR committed 22 billion euros to Italy's telecoms network. Jannik Sinner announced his knee injury ends his 2026 season.
